data.name: Nageshwar
data.gender_notes: Nageshwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nageshwar is a name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'Lord of Serpents'. It is a revered name in Hindu mythology, associated with Lord Shiva who is often depicted with serpents as his companions or adornments. The name Nageshwar carries the meaning “Lord of Serpents” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nageshwar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of serpents and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nageshwar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Serpents.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nageshwar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Lord Shiva as Nageswara is vastly celebrated in various parts of India, especially during the annual Shiva Ratri festival. This symbolizes the victory of good over evil, as Lord Shiva is depicted subduing the powerful serpent, Vasuki.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nageshwar holds deep spiritual significance for many Hindus, as it represents the transformation and mastery over negative emotions or fears represented by serpents. It is a reminder to seek protection and power from the supreme Lord Shiva, who can help us overcome our inner demons and live a peaceful and virtuous life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nageshwar is a name revered in Hinduism, symbolizing the divine protector and destroyer of sorrows andignorance. The 'Naga' in Nageshwar signifies the serpent form of Lord Shiva, embodying wisdom and healing, while 'Ishwar' signifies the supreme ruler and god of the universe.

historical_references.reference: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, Nageshwar is believed to be situated in Dwarka, Gujarat. The legend goes that Lord Shiva, in the form of a Naga (serpent), saved the Devas from the wrath of Indra. In gratitude, Indra built the temple at Dwarka.

Another belief associates Nageshwar with the Pandavas from the Mahabharata. During their 12-year exile, the Pandavas built a Shiva temple at each of the twelve Jyotirlingas, including Nageshwar. The temple is located at Rameshwar in Dwarka district, Gujarat.

modern_usage.modern_context: Nageshwar is a revered Hindu deity, particularly in the Indian subcontinent, known for his association with Naga serpents. He is worshipped in various temples, especially in the Indian states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Gujarat. In the modern context, Nageshwar is a popular topic on social media, blogs, and travel websites. People share pictures and stories of their visits to Nageshwar temples, seek blessings and guidance, and engage in spiritual discussions related to Hindu deities and Nageshwar's significance. The deity's association with Naga serpents and the natural beauty surrounding many of his temples also make him a favorite among travelers.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Nageshwar, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Nageshwar meaning "Lord of Serpents" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
